scope: Model S/A Pd/L-pGlu stereochemical productive-reactivity comparison, and isolated S/1b and P/3ba inversion at their respective source conditions; bounded relation to shared experimental observations.
guidance_markdown:
# Author hypothesis and method baseline

The author labels 1b, 2a and 3ba correspond to public S, A and P. Labels a/b distinguish the two substrate configurations and do not by themselves specify absolute stereochemistry. Establish a structural mapping before comparing them.

The authors hypothesize that nitrogen interconversion and differential productive reactivity participate in dynamic kinetic resolution. Their catalytic model combines Pd(OAc)2 with L-pyroglutamic acid, binds the pyridyl-directed substrate, and examines a concerted metalation/deprotonation (CMD) step connecting 19 to 21 through TS20 for both configurations. Later modeled events include coordination rearrangement, alkene coordination/insertion and beta-hydrogen elimination. The current comparison centers on the two substrate pathways and isolated-molecule configurational interconversion; a full cycle, catalyst oxidation or a coordinated-interconversion mechanism is not required. Test the hypothesis rather than assuming a rate- or selectivity-determining assignment.

The source used Gaussian 16; geometries and frequencies at B3LYP with def2-SVP on Pd and 6-31G(d) on other elements; M06-2X single points with def2-TZVP on Pd and 6-311+G(d,p) on other elements; SMD solvation; and Shermo thermal corrections at 363.15 K for the catalytic S/A model. The stated assembly is E_elec + E_sol + G_corr. IRC calculations were used to check transition-state connections. The early catalytic states use the same initial-state energy reference. For a pair of stereochemical TSs with identical composition, common spectator and reference terms cancel; do not confuse their energy separation with the difference of two local barriers from different bound intermediates.

For isolated S and P interconversion the reported electronic treatment is M06-2X/6-311+G(d,p)/SMD//B3LYP/6-31G(d). Preserve S in acetonitrile at 353.15 K and P in n-octane at 398.15 K, distinct from the catalytic temperature and solvent. These calculations alone cannot establish reaction-condition interconversion kinetics. Relating them to a rate requires an explicit physical model and its assumptions; no additional coordinated-interconversion calculation is imposed.

The SI contains Cartesian coordinates (Data S3, starting printed S174), molecular drawings and relative-energy profiles. Data S2 contains X-ray crystallographic data. Raw electronic-structure inputs, frequency/IRC output files and a complete per-state electronic/thermal energy table were not located in the inspected source. The source method summary does not state all charge/multiplicity inputs, Shermo low-frequency settings, standard-state adjustments or convergence/grid choices. Declare reconstruction choices; do not attribute unreported settings to the authors. Rebuild and validate the states used in your claims. The neutral organic interconversion models are closed-shell reconstructions from their molecular graphs; verify the relevant Pd-model electronic state. No energy value, winning configuration, numerical rate or final mechanistic conclusion is supplied here.
status: Disclosed methods and hypotheses only; author result values and ordering are private.
